title: Finite affine coproduct descent presentation of a locally constant pro-etale sheaf
statement:
Let $X$ be a qcqs scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $S$ be a set in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $F$ be a sheaf of sets [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Suppose a pro-étale covering $\{U_i\to X\}$ is supplied with isomorphisms $F|_{U_i}\simeq\underline S_{U_i}$, where $\underline S$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf with value $S$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf].

There exist finitely many affine pro-étale objects $V_j\to X$, each mapping over $X$ to one of the $U_i$, such that $V=\coprod_jV_j$ is affine and $p:V\to X$ is weakly étale, flat, surjective and quasi-compact, and $\{p\}$ is both an fpqc and a pro-étale covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. There is a trivialization $\psi:F|_V\simeq\underline S_V$. Let $T=\coprod_{s\in S}V$, the scheme coproduct [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. For every weakly étale $W\to V$ there are natural bijections $F(W)\simeq\underline S_V(W)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_V(W,T)$, taking a constant label to its component section. The latter functor is a sheaf and its sections are precisely the $S$-indexed clopen decompositions of $W$ (pairwise disjoint open subschemes whose union is $W$).

Put $R=V\times_XV$ and let $p_1,p_2:R\to V$ be its projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. The transition between the two pullbacks of $\psi$ is induced by a unique $R$-isomorphism $\delta:p_1^*T\xrightarrow{\sim}p_2^*T$. For each fixed source label $s$, its target labels give a clopen decomposition of $R$, and on its piece labelled $t$ the map is the identity of that open subscheme from component $s$ to component $t$. These component maps assemble to $\delta$, its inverse realizes the inverse transition, and $\delta_{13}=\delta_{23}\circ\delta_{12}$ on $V\times_XV\times_XV$. Thus it is a scheme descent datum [def-pd-descent-datum] realizing the restrictions of $F$. Empty $X$ and empty $S$ are allowed.

proof.text: For nonempty X use finite_affine_proetale_refinement, retaining its affine opens and maps to the supplied charts. For empty X use Fin 0 and the empty covering. Form the actual finite scheme coproduct. IsZariskiLocalAtSource.sigmaDesc proves its codiagonal weakly etale; the finite affine coproduct instance makes its source affine. The refinement cover proves joint surjectivity. Compactness of the source and quasi-separatedness of X imply quasi-compactness, and Hom.singleton_mem_propQCPrecoverage supplies the singleton pro-etale cover and hence the fpqc cover. The explicit universes keep the schemes, label set, and their coproducts in Type u, with sheaf values lifted to Type (u + 1).

proof.text: Restriction along a weakly etale map is precomposition. Its pushforwardContinuousSheafificationCompatibility identifies the restriction of a constant sheaf with the constant sheaf and gives the restriction of each supplied trivialization to its affine chart. Pulling back the disjoint summand inclusions gives a disjoint open cover of every test object. Sheaf amalgamation identifies sections with the product of the sections on these pieces: distinct pieces have empty common test source, where sheaf sections are terminal. Conjugating the product of the restricted trivializations gives the trivialization on the coproduct. This argument includes an empty family.

proof.text: Map the constant presheaf to this representable by component sections. The coproduct clopen-description theorem shows local surjectivity on the component preimages. Equality of two distinct labels forces the test scheme empty, where the empty covering proves local injectivity. Lift the map by sheafifyLift and use the local-bijection composition criteria and Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso. The factorization through toSheafify proves the required label equation. The same coproduct theorem supplies the clopen decomposition and unique Over morphism for every test object.

proof.text: The codiagonal from the coproduct of copies is weakly etale by source locality, so it is a pro-etale site object Q. The slice equivalence and the trivialization and constant-model comparison identify F.over V with sliceTo.op composed with uliftYoneda Q. Construct the comparison at Q times_X V: its universal Q-point gives a section of F via the first lift and a Q-point via the second. An arbitrary point and second lift map to this universal test scheme, defining transport without choosing a witness. Pullback functoriality proves naturality, and naturality of the representing isomorphism proves compatibility with F sections.

proof.text: Test transport_self on Q itself and transport_transport on Q times_X V times_X V; these are weakly etale objects over X. Compatibility identifies all transports with the same section of F, proving both identities there. Every arbitrary point and collection of lifts factors through these universal objects; naturality pulls back the identities. Package these maps and laws into the existing Over.DescentDatum. Applying the inverse representing isomorphism gives the stated HEq compatibility, with identity maps of the underlying scheme identifying equal composites to X.

proof.text: For any pair r1,r2 with equal composite to X, transport the universal point of pullback r1 T and apply Over.mapPullbackAdj r2 to obtain a morphism to pullback r2 T. Transport naturality gives its realization identity on every scheme point. The reverse transport and the cocycle and identity laws give its two inverse equations. Testing any other realizing isomorphism on the universal source point, and using pullback extensionality, proves uniqueness. This directly implements the mapping-property step without a separate Yoneda full-faithfulness application.

proof.text: Evaluate transport on each source-label section and apply coproductCopiesMorphismsClopen to its underlying morphism over the overlap. This supplies both displayed clopen transition conditions. Combine the finite-cover witnesses, trivialization, constant-model comparison, clopen mapping property, compatible datum, and unique transition isomorphism. Empty labels and empty schemes were retained throughout.
